text:
People say, rumor has it, in drawing rooms, at parties, some person or persons in the know insist that Jaime Sabines is a great poet. Or at least a good poet. Or a decent, worthy poet. Or simply, but truly, a poet.


Jaime gets the news and is delighted: how wonderful! I'm a poet! I'm an important poet! I'm a great poet!


Convinced, he goes out into the street, or arrives home, convinced. But in the street nobody, and at home even less: nobody notices he's a poet. Why don't poets have a star on their foreheads, or a visible glow, or a ray coming out of their ears?


My God! Jaime says. I have to be a dad or a husband, or work in the factory like anyone else, or walk around like anyone else, a pedestrian.


That's it! Jaime says. I'm not a poet: I'm a pedestrian.


And this time he stays lying in bed with a sweet, quiet joy.

translation.title: The Pedestrian
